Earthworm: One continuous segmented pink-brown tube in a gentle noncrossing curve, clitellum near the broad right anterior end and narrow left posterior. No limbs, eyes or invented head features. Both ends complete; glossy surface needs painted-style review and body-to-ground contact remains authoring-specific.
Sponge: Single irregular golden porous vase with large open osculum and continuous basal tissue; no head, limbs or invented face. Fine pitted texture reads more photographic than the approved brushwork in places, so style remains a hold. Basal projections are tissue, not declared feet; no seabed painted.
Snail: Complete coiled brown shell, continuous wide muscular foot, two separate long eye-bearing tentacles and two lower feelers. The mouth below the head is not unambiguously separable from the foot/head fold at this view; retain mouth-ownership hold rather than inventing a joint. Surface is very glossy and needs painted-style review.
Mussel: Two dark blue-black growth-lined wedge valves open at a narrow left hinge area, mantle tissue and fine byssal threads. A large pale tongue-like foot protrudes to the right; its scale/shape and hinge placement need biological review rather than automatic acceptance. No eyes or paired siphon tubes. Open valve pose is wider than the requested slight opening.
